articles.title: McConnell may block his conservative critic's year-end ambassadorial confirmation
articles.author: Burgess Everett
articles.summary: The Scoop Mitch McConnell may knock former Kentucky Senate candidate Nate Morris’ nomination as ambassador to Colombia out of the Senate’s year-end nominations package, a move that could imperil the McConnell critic’s bid to join the Trump administration. The Kentucky senator has not signed off on Morris’ addition to a large group of executive branch nominees, according to two people familiar with the discussions. His office said that he hasn’t made a final decision. “Senator McConnell will evaluate the en bloc package when it is presented to the conference,” said David Popp, a spokesperson for McConnell, who’s retiring at the end of the year. Morris ran for Senate this cycle before endorsing Andy Barr, who won the seat in November; the ally of Donald Trump Jr. was then tapped as ambassador to Colombia by President Donald Trump. His nomination advanced to the Senate floor earlier this month, but he may not get a standalone vote given the limited floor time remaining for the last days of the Republican majority.
